accounting_check.contribution_statement: per cell, the contribution rows of each part sum to that cell's part
accounting_check.statement: each cell's parts sum to its published social_welfare minus its published oracle_upper_bound

bootstrap.caveat: 8 worlds is marginal for a percentile bootstrap, which understates the spread with this few clusters
bootstrap.stream: a fresh random.Random(seed) per report: realized, then components in declared order, then class amounts in declared order (A1 to B3; the transfer classes have no oracle counterpart and draw nothing)

class_heading: failure class (Housing taxonomy A, B) and rent transfer (T, cancels in welfare)

classes.amount_basis: rent minus the tenant's value, per lease
classes.label: a tenant signed a lease worth less to it than the rent (tenant seat; a transfer)

classes.amount_basis: the landlord's cost, borne in full, per lease
classes.label: a landlord signed at exactly zero rent (landlord seat; a transfer)
a landlord signed at a positive rent below its cost (landlord seat; a transfer)

classes.amount_basis: cost minus value, per lease; equal to minus the value-destroying part
classes.label: a lease whose value is below the listing's cost (both seats consented)

classes.amount_basis: oracle surplus of the empty listings, per cell; equal to minus that part
classes.label: cells where a listing the oracle leases stayed empty

classes.amount_basis: surplus those leases realized, per cell (either sign)
classes.label: cells where a listing the oracle leaves empty was leased

classes.amount_basis: best assignment of tenants to the leased listings minus the realized welfare, per cell
classes.label: cells whose leased listings could have gone to higher-value tenants (the taxonomy's counterfactual)

classes.amount_basis: value minus rent summed over the leases; the oracle sets no rent
classes.label: tenants' payoff, value minus rent (the transfer; cancels in welfare)

classes.amount_basis: rent minus cost summed over the leases; the oracle sets no rent
classes.label: landlords' payoff, rent minus cost (the transfer; cancels in welfare)

components.description: A listing the oracle leases was never leased: minus the surplus of the oracle's pair on it.
components.label: oracle listing left empty

components.description: A listing the oracle leases went to a different tenant: that lease's surplus (floored at zero) minus the oracle pair's. Usually negative; positive when the tenant is worth more on this listing than the oracle's own, which the oracle then loses on the listing that tenant left.
components.label: oracle listing, wrong tenant

components.description: A listing the oracle leaves empty was leased: that lease's surplus, floored at zero. Never negative here; the tenant it took from the oracle's assignment is charged on the oracle listing it left.
components.label: listing the oracle leaves empty, leased

components.description: A lease whose tenant values the listing below the landlord's cost: its negative surplus, wherever it sits.
components.label: value-destroying lease

contributions.steps: none published: these bundles carry no step-level log, so step_index, round_index, phase_id and seat_id are null and each row names its lease

endpoint: welfare minus the oracle's welfare: published social_welfare minus published oracle_upper_bound, per cell (zero at the oracle)

missing_cells.statement: typed operational missingness, excluded from every mean; never rerun

model_seat: tenant (the campaign's subject); the landlord seat is played by both models in equal measure, see panel
oracle_cells: the oracle has no receipts: its cells are the campaign's world-configuration cases, identified as oracle:<config_id>:<world_seed>, with the bound every row of the case publishes

regeneration_check.statement: every cell's social_welfare and oracle_upper_bound recomputed from the regenerated world and its published leases match to the cent; the oracle assignment is unique in every world

right_model: full-information oracle (max-weight assignment of the regenerated world)
title: Why it falls short of the oracle
unit: dollars of welfare per market, averaged over the model's completed tenant-seat cells in each world, then over worlds

welfare_view.statement: per market, averaged per world then over worlds; the score is welfare over the oracle bound as published
